history.dynasty: Legendary (Kritayuga sthala-purana); existing structures attributed to 15th-17th century, with 1626 AD construction by devotee Devulapalli Achyutabagavantulu per one source
history.period: Purana-era legend; archaeological evidence of temple and pushkarini from the 15th century; 1626 AD
history.summary: Hilltop Lakshmi Narasimha temple on Sobhanadri (Sobhanagiri) hill at Agiripalli, about 25 km from Vijayawada; the deity is also known as Sri Sobhanachaleswara Swamy. The temple's own site claims puranic antiquity of about 4000 years, while archaeological evidence is cited from the 15th century, and one account credits Devulapalli Achyutabagavantulu with building the temple in 1626 AD -- conflicting dates flagged (verify). Devotees climb 740 steps (no ghat road). The Varaha Pushkarini (Ananta Sarasu) is believed to have been dug by Mahavishnu as Adi Varaha; its water is used for pujas. In 1561 a devotee laid out a garden and Bhoga Mantapam whose flowers were once sent to the Bhadrachalam Sita Rama temple. CSV town corrected: Vijayawada -> Agiripalli (the temple is at Agiripalli; Vijayawada is the nearest city). Coordinates are from the temple's map listing, corroborated by geocoding Agiripalli. name: Sri Vyagra Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple, Agiripalli
town_description: Agiripalli is a town and mandal headquarters in Eluru district of Andhra Pradesh, about 25 km from Vijayawada. It is best known for the hilltop Lakshmi Narasimha (Sobhanachaleswara) temple on Sobhanadri hill, and serves as a local market and administrative centre for surrounding villages.
tradition: Vaishnavism (Lakshmi Narasimha worship; the hill's legend also associates Shiva with the site)

travel.airport: Vijayawada International Airport at Gannavaram (about 20 km, per temple travel guides)
travel.railway: Vijayawada Junction (about 29 km, per temple travel guides)
travel.road: About 25-30 km from Vijayawada by road; direct buses run from Vijayawada to Agiripalli; 740 steps climb to the hilltop shrine, no ghat road

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Maghotsavam (January-February) for the main festival
